transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-08
Time: 15:00 - 15:48 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Lena Park (Redwood Solutions), Dana Ortiz (SilverMantle Platform), Samir Patel (SilverMantle SRE), Priya Nair (SilverMantle Security), Jonas (DevOps)

[00:00:00] Alyssa Chen: okay everyone good afternoon, um thanks for joining. quick agenda - helm operator packaging, k r m s key flow, marketplace listing constraints, and next steps. Marco will lead the operator bit.
[00:00:23] Marco Ruiz: hey all, yeah i'll start. so we, we built a lightweight helm operator that installs the LLM gateway as a k8s operator. it exposes a CRD called llmgateway.svc.redwood.dev, and you can define modelRoutes, routingPolicy, and kmsConfig. note: CRD name in the repo atm has a typo in some samples - llmgatewy - sorry we'll fix that.
[00:01:05] Dana Ortiz: oh okay that's the sort of thing we run into, ty. question: does the operator require cluster-admin? we can't give that in staging.
[00:01:23] Marco Ruiz: good call. no cluster-admin needed for the chart if you use the namespaced install. there is an optional nodeAffinity webhook that requires additional privileges; we can disable that in values.yaml. default permissions are limited to the namespace and create/watch on the CRD resources.
[00:01:50] Priya Nair: and from a security perspective we need to ensure the operator never logs plaintext keys. where do tokens live?
[00:02:04] Marco Ruiz: tokens are stored in k8s secrets by default. we support sealed-secrets and external KMS integrations where you can provide a kmsConfig referencing an external keyArn. we also have a sidecar that will rotate attach tokens on a schedule. small note: the sidecar rotation code path uses a short-lived service token (60s) - that's something we need to document better.
[00:02:36] Samir Patel: rotation sounds good. how about metrics? we need per-route latency percentiles and per-model cost tags for billing.
[00:02:50] Lena Park: yes, our telemetry exports prometheus metrics and we can emit token-level cost tags as labels on the request span. we also support pushing traces to jaeger or honeycomb. but tag cardinality is a concern, so we usually recommend sampling for high-cardinality user_id labels.
[00:03:20] Jonas: quick interruption — which KMS are we talking? AWS? we have a hybrid environment, some keys on cloudhsm.
[00:03:31] Priya Nair: yeah we use AWS KMS + internal HSM for PII workflows. the marketplace listing requires that private keys never leave customer boundary per our governance.
[00:03:48] Marco Ruiz: understood. we support both AWS KMS and PKCS11 HSM integrations. for onprem HSM we have a connector that uses the kmsConfig with type: pkcs11 and you mount socket to the operator. the operator itself doesn't export key material, it only sends signing requests to the HSM. note: the PKCS11 path is relatively new and the docs are a bit sparse.
[00:04:22] [00:04:24] Dana Ortiz: can we see an example policy for the KMS key so our compliance folks can sign off?
[00:04:30] Alyssa Chen: yes, marco will share a minimal policy snippet after the call. (inaudible) i'll add that to next steps.
[00:04:45] Marco Ruiz: i'll dump the example — it's basically kms:Encrypt,Decrypt for the operator role plus kms:GenerateDataKey when using envelope encryption. we'll include a least-privilege sample.
[00:05:05] Samir Patel: another operational question - what happens if the gateway can't reach hosted Redwood model endpoints? we need graceful fallback to a cheaper quantized local model to preserve availability.
[00:05:21] Marco Ruiz: good question. there are two strategies we recommend: 1) route policy with failover: primary route to hosted redwood api, secondary to a local quantized variant running in the same cluster, 2) local inference sidecar that keeps a tiny LLM cache (prefix cache) for high-frequency prompts. both require you to add a modelVariant config in the CRD. the fallback is synchronous and respects SLOs but adds some latency — we measured +70–180ms depending on the quantized runtime.
[00:06:02] Dana Ortiz: latency delta is acceptable, but we need to quantify cost. any estimate for token cost difference?
[00:06:10] Lena Park: hosted calls are metered per-token, local quantized model is mostly infra cost. rough ballpark: hosted ~ $0.0008 per token for our curated model profile, local infra depends on GPU utilization; for small quantized models on CPU it's maybe $0.00005 per token equivalent, but that's very workload dependent. we'll share a cost worksheet.
[00:06:38] [00:06:45] Priya Nair: for marketplace listing, we also need audit logs that show the request path and key usage without exposing prompt content. is there an obfuscation or hashing feature?
[00:06:57] Marco Ruiz: yes we have a redact middleware you can enable that hashes PII fields or replaces text with tokens before logs are emitted. it runs as part of the gateway filter chain. caveat: if you redact too aggressively you may hamper quality monitoring.
[00:07:20] Jonas: how are we publishing billing meter tags to the marketplace? we need to attach partner and customer ids so the marketplace can attribute usage.
[00:07:30] Alyssa Chen: the gateway emits billing headers and usage tags as HTTP headers and Bookkeeping metrics. we can configure partner_id in the CRD values and the operator will ensure all spawned pods have the env var for meter tagging. note: we added a recent change so tags are also included in the prometheus exporter.
[00:07:55] Samir Patel: we saw a prior note in the repo about prefix cache and memory leaks in k8s 1.24. are you patched for that?
[00:08:05] Marco Ruiz: yes we tracked a leak pattern in the prefetcher; fixed in v0.9.2 of the operator. recommend upgrading to >=0.9.2. the helm chart in the repo will default to that. we'll call out the k8s compatibility matrix in the README.
[00:08:30] [00:08:34] Dana Ortiz: good, we run 1.24 in staging. next: marketplace listing constraints — we have to limit runtime container images to scanned SBOMs and restrict network egress. how does the operator help with that?
[00:08:49] Marco Ruiz: operator can enforce image policies via an admission webhook (optional) and we support supply-chain attestation fields in the Chart metadata. for egress we provide a per-model egressPolicy that you can set to internal-only or allowlist endpoints. the egressPolicy will be enforced by the operator's sidecar network proxy.
[00:09:20] Priya Nair: for the allowlist, we need a pattern that doesn't hardcode endpoints because our infra sits behind a private NAT. can we do CIDR ranges instead?
[00:09:30] Marco Ruiz: yes the egressPolicy accepts CIDR ranges and service names; we also support a service mesh compatibility mode where we rely on the mesh egress rules.
[00:09:44] [00:09:50] Lena Park: on quantization tradeoffs, i want to call out that 4-bit quant gives smaller memory but may slightly degrade hallucination rates on longer contexts. for the marketplace we recommend evaluating with your eval-set and we'll provide a quant profile suggestion table.
[00:10:10] Dana Ortiz: speaking of evals, can we wire our pre-existing prompt suite into Redwood's eval harness?
[00:10:19] Marco Ruiz: yes there's an adapter. send us the prompt pack (a csv or jsonl) and we can run a quick sweep comparing hosted vs quantized local. expect results in 48–72 hours for a starter set.
[00:10:40] Jonas: small ops question — what's the rollout story for new model versions? we need canary plus auto rollback on latency regressions.
[00:10:51] Marco Ruiz: built-in rollout supports canary percent and automated rollback if latency or error budget thresholds are breached. we integrate with your existing alerting (pagerduty slack) and you can configure SLOs in the CRD.
[00:11:10] [00:11:30] Samir Patel: network secrets - do you recommend vault or k8s native? we are heavy on HashiCorp Vault.
[00:11:40] Marco Ruiz: both supported. operator has a Vault provider that will sync secrets into k8s as projected volumes; you can choose short-lived tokens. for compliance we often recommend vault with dynamic creds.
[00:11:59] Priya Nair: wanna call out an audit ask — can we get an event stream with KMS key usage events in near-real time so our auditors can reconcile?
[00:12:12] Lena Park: yes we provide a usage export that can push to an S3 bucket or to your SIEM via Kinesis. it includes key operation stamped events but we can filter prompt content.
[00:12:30] [00:12:46] Dana Ortiz: thanks. i'd like to walk through a proposed minimal staging install. Marco?
[00:12:53] Marco Ruiz: sure - step 1: helm repo add redwood; step 2: values.yaml minimal: namespace: sm-staging, enableWebhook: false, kmsConfig: { type: "aws_kms", keyArn: "<placeholder>" }, modelRoutes: [ { name: "default", model: "redwood/fast-13b", route: "hosted" } ] — note: the transcript sample here includes braces — in the shared notes we'll provide a full values file.
[00:13:30] Jonas: will that deploy a sidecar or a daemonset?
[00:13:35] Marco Ruiz: it's a deployment per gateway instance; sidecars are injected as part of the pod template. for cache-heavy workloads we recommend a small statefulset for the cache component.
[00:13:50] [00:13:57] Alyssa Chen: i'll pause for a sec — any blockers for you to proceed with staging?
[00:14:03] Dana Ortiz: two blockers: 1) need the KMS policy example, 2) need SBOM and image scan evidence for the container.
[00:14:11] Alyssa Chen: we can provide both. Marco will send KMS policy; Lena will attach the SBOM and the recent scan report.
[00:14:22] Lena Park: i'll upload SBOM and a short explanation of our CI scan in the shared drive. note: some of the images are based on distroless slices and buildinfo may be noisy.
[00:14:37] [00:14:45] Samir Patel: curious about latency SLOs — do you have sample dashboards we can import?
[00:14:52] Marco Ruiz: yes, Grafana dashboard json is in the repo /dashboards/llm_gateway.json. it includes per-route p50/p95/p99 and token counts. we'll share a preconfigured dashboard link.
[00:15:12] Dana Ortiz: perfect. quick question about marketplace listing governance — our legal needs an exportable audit report showing which customer used which model and when, without revealing prompts. is that feasible?
[00:15:25] Priya Nair: also need to be able to revoke access to a specific partner ID quickly.
[00:15:32] Marco Ruiz: both doable. audit export includes model_id, partner_id, request_hash, and timestamps; request_hash lets you correlate without storing content. partner revocation is a simple CRD update to remove partner_id or mark partner_id as suspended; operator will reconcile and remove env vars from pods; for immediate cut we can implement a network policy pivot.
[00:15:58] [00:16:05] Jonas: are there any known performance regressions when running under CRI-O vs containerd?
[00:16:14] Marco Ruiz: minimal differences; our testing matrix covers both. CRI-O had one sporadic pod restart in older k8s versions due to log driver assumptions but that's fixed in recent images. we'll note compatibility in the README.
[00:16:40] [00:17:00] Alyssa Chen: ok we're mid-call — i'm going to cover the pilot scope and success criteria quickly. pilot: staged helm operator install, kms policy validation, run a 24h synthetic workload with 10 qps, measure p95 latency and cost baseline. success = p95 < 250ms (hosted) and fallback effective < 400ms and audit exports validate.
[00:17:30] Dana Ortiz: those success criteria seem reasonable. what about data residency — some requests must never leave eu-west region.
[00:17:42] Marco Ruiz: routingPolicy supports regionAffinity; you can pin routes to endpoints in eu-west and failover to eu-west quantized variant. for marketplace listing we recommend adding region metadata to the modelRoute CRD and the operator will enforce region locality.
[00:18:05] [00:18:20] Priya Nair: small nit — the CRD example we saw earlier had a camelCase mix; our linting wants snake_case. can you provide both?
[00:18:31] Marco Ruiz: yeah we actually provide both in examples; the parser accepts either but README will standardize to snake_case. thanks for the callout.
[00:18:45] [00:19:00] Lena Park: another thought on cost: when evaluating quantized variants we recommend tracking hallucination metrics (F1-style on your evals) in addition to token cost - sometimes the lower-cost model increases manual review overhead.
[00:19:20] Dana Ortiz: okay — good reminder. next, around the marketplace onboarding checklist — what items should we expect from Redwood?
[00:19:31] Alyssa Chen: we'll provide: helm chart + values.yaml, SBOM and scan report, KMS policy snippet, Grafana dashboard json, pilot SOW template, and a short runbook for cutover.
[00:19:45] Samir Patel: and from us: staging namespace access, KMS key ARN or HSM contact, existing prompt test suite, and a compliance contact for signoff.
[00:19:58] [00:20:10] Jonas: how about integration tests — do you have a CI harness we can run that validates install and smoke tests?
[00:20:18] Marco Ruiz: yes, we have a GH Action that runs chart install in KinD and a smoke curl test. it's in .github/workflows/helm-smoke.yml. it doesn't exercise production scale but it catches install regressions.
[00:20:35] [00:20:48] Dana Ortiz: can we get the action to run against our chart repo mirror?
[00:20:54] Lena Park: you can fork the repo and enable the actions, or we can add a repo_dispatch to trigger from your pipeline — both options possible.
[00:21:10] [00:21:20] Alyssa Chen: ok we're coming up on the second half — any deep technical blockers left?
[00:21:26] Priya Nair: KMS policy + SBOM scan are the primary blockers for compliance sign-off. after those we can proceed to install.
[00:21:36] Marco Ruiz: i'll attach the policy and the helm values. quick note: the helm chart includes a toggle for attestation and supply-chain metadata.
[00:21:49] Dana Ortiz: for the pilot workload, what sample size do you recommend for evals? 1k prompts?
[00:21:57] Lena Park: start with 1k diverse prompts. we'll run both hosted and local and produce a delta table showing accuracy, latency, and cost per prompt bucket.
[00:22:10] [00:22:30] Samir Patel: can we also test a canary with sticky sessions? some of our flows rely on maintaining KV cache across chat turns.
[00:22:38] Marco Ruiz: yes the gateway supports sticky-session affinity via a session cookie or header. you can configure KV cache TTL per-route. we'll include a sample canary config.
[00:22:55] Dana Ortiz: what about secrets rotation cadence? we prefer automatic rotation every 7 days.
[00:23:02] Marco Ruiz: sidecar rotation supports configurable cadence; default is 7 days in the operator values.
[00:23:15] [00:23:30] Alyssa Chen: i'm going to summarize the concrete next steps we agreed on — Marco to share helm chart + values + dashboard + KMS policy by 2026-09-10; Lena to share SBOM + scan report in shared drive by 2026-09-10; SilverMantle (Priya/Dana) to share KMS ARN and compliance contacts by 2026-09-14; schedule runbook dry-run week of 2026-09-21. does that capture?
[00:23:57] Dana Ortiz: yes, capture that. Also please include the eval adapter instructions so we can upload the prompt set.
[00:24:05] Alyssa Chen: will do.
[00:24:12] [00:24:20] Lena Park: small follow up — i'll add quantization profile suggestions for your eval set in the shared notes.
[00:24:30] Jonas: one last ops question — if we want to pin to a specific model version, can we do automated migration with traffic splitting?
[00:24:39] Marco Ruiz: yes, the route CRD supports traffic weights. you can do 90/10 split and progressively shift; rollback is automatic if SLOs break.
[00:24:55] [00:25:10] Alyssa Chen: great — looks like we're aligned. any other questions from SilverMantle?
[00:25:16] Priya Nair: just one procedural — we need a short statement of data residency and encryption-at-rest for the marketplace listing doc.
[00:25:26] Alyssa Chen: we'll include that in the SOW. Marco, Lena - can we add that?
[00:25:33] Marco Ruiz: yes we'll add a one-paragraph statement about region affinity and default encryption using KMS/HSM.
[00:25:44] [00:26:00] Dana Ortiz: thanks team. we'll aim to run the smoke install next week once we have the helm chart.
[00:26:08] Alyssa Chen: perfect. last note — pricing: there was a question earlier about Dedicated vs Hosted cost delta. i'll follow up with a short matrix after this call.
[00:26:22] Samir Patel: okay thanks.
[00:26:28] [00:26:35] Alyssa Chen: all right if nothing else we'll wrap. thanks everyone for the time.
[00:26:40] Marco Ruiz: thanks all.
[00:26:45] Dana Ortiz: thank you.
[00:26:49] [End of recorded transcript]
